us.h: House shelves Massie's bid to impeach Hegseth
us.s: In a 211-204 vote Tuesday, the House sent Massie's eight impeachment articles over the Iran war and boat strikes to the Judiciary Committee, which effectively kills them this Congress. Massie was the lone Republican opposed.

us.h: Mississippi Senate race still too close to call
us.s: With 98% counted, Democrat Scott Colom leads GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith by about 3,000 votes. Some mail and affidavit ballots are still outstanding, counties must certify by Nov. 13, and state law bars recounts.

us.h: White House counsel warns Democrats over oversight threats
us.s: In a letter, White House counsel Will Scharf told Rep. Robert Garcia, who is in line to lead House Oversight, that Democrats' planned probes of the administration could cross into criminal conduct.

us.h: Bessent moves to military base after reported Iranian threat
us.s: After a reported Iranian threat on his life, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has moved from his D.C.-area home onto a military base. His department says he will keep up sanctions pressure on Tehran.

us.h: Sanders says he won't back Schumer as Democratic leader
us.s: Bernie Sanders says he won't support Chuck Schumer as leader and wants an open debate on the party's direction. Chris Van Hollen is weighing a challenge. The vote is expected in early December.

us.h: House GOP report faults decades of failures on Epstein
us.s: Comer's Oversight Committee released a 137-page report blaming federal prosecutors and investigators for missteps that let Epstein keep abusing victims. It urges the Justice Department to reinterview witnesses and look into his associates.

world.h: Russia, Ukraine agree to large prisoner swap; no breakthrough
world.s: U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi ended with a deal on a major POW exchange but no wider progress. Kushner and Witkoff plan to meet Putin in Moscow Thursday, then Zelenskyy in Dublin.

world.h: Spain holds first general strike in 14 years
world.s: Unions shut down work across Spain to protest housing costs, wages and prices. There were roadblocks in Barcelona and scuffles near Madrid's wholesale market. A national election is set for Nov. 29.

world.h: Hoax bomb threats hit thousands of European schools
world.s: At least 6,300 Italian schools, plus hundreds in Ireland and the U.K., got emailed bomb threats, prompting evacuations. Nothing was found. Officials suspect hybrid-warfare tactics but have named no culprit.

world.h: U.S. Army officer arrested in UK over Russia spying
world.s: British police arrested a 41-year-old U.S. soldier near Gloucester on suspicion of espionage linked to Russia. A U.S. official said he is a senior officer at a NATO corps headquarters.

world.h: Guterres presses COP31 to phase out fossil fuels
world.s: Speaking at COP31 in Antalya, the UN chief blamed the fossil fuel lobby for stalling climate action and called for ending coal, oil and gas. The U.S. and several G7 leaders are staying away.

world.h: Russia says it downed 146 drones near St. Petersburg
world.s: The Leningrad region's governor says 146 drones were shot down and one strike started a fire near Ust-Luga port. Latvia and Lithuania told residents to take shelter from drones entering their airspace.

tech.h: Nvidia customer Megaspeed's empty offices deepen China questions
tech.s: CBS found Megaspeed's Singapore headquarters nearly empty. The firm, tied to the woman linked to Jensen Huang, bought about $4.8 billion of Nvidia gear and is under investigation in the U.S. and Singapore.

tech.h: New York opens registration under its AI safety law
tech.s: Large frontier AI developers such as OpenAI and Anthropic must register with New York by Jan. 1. Starting in 2027, the RAISE Act requires safety frameworks and incident reports within 72 hours.

tech.h: NRC approves X-energy's first small modular reactors
tech.s: Regulators approved a construction permit for four Xe-100 reactors at a Dow plant in Texas, the first advanced reactor approval at a U.S. industrial site. They won't run until the early 2030s.

tech.h: Anthropic's seven founders to sell about $250M each in IPO
tech.s: A new filing shows each co-founder selling about 3.38 million shares in the IPO. Together they keep 51.1% of voting power through special Class F shares.

tech.h: Oura to buy AI primary-care startup Counsel for $625M
tech.s: The smart-ring maker is buying Counsel Health, which pairs AI chat with licensed doctors, after shelving its own IPO plans. Counsel's CEO will become Oura's chief clinical AI officer.

tech.h: German regulator says PayPal surcharge ban may hurt competition
tech.s: In preliminary findings, Germany's Federal Cartel Office said PayPal's ban on merchant surcharges may be unlawful and keep its fees high. PayPal disagrees and could be made to hand over profits.

talking.h: Vikings bring back Kirk Cousins in deadline trade
talking.s: Minnesota sent a 2027 third-round pick to Las Vegas for Cousins, 38, who returns to the team he played for from 2018 to 2023. The Vikings' offense has struggled despite a top-ranked defense.

talking.h: Stacy Keach, TV's Mike Hammer, dies at 85
talking.s: Keach died at his home in Poland after a long fight with heart failure, his wife said. He played detective Mike Hammer on TV, won a Golden Globe and earned a Tony nomination.

coming.s: The BLS publishes October wholesale inflation at 8:30 a.m. ET, following this week's hotter consumer price report.

coming.h: Mississippi counties' deadline to certify Senate vote
coming.s: Counties must certify results in the tight Colom vs. Hyde-Smith race. The state allows no recounts, so the plurality wins.
The Census Bureau's advance retail sales estimate comes out at 8:30 a.m. ET, an early look at consumer spending heading into the holidays.
